messages:
AutoPagingBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> service: inference-hosted | rule: p99-latency-east | severity: P1 | SLO burn: 125% (5m). Incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345

PagerDuty Bot: Incident created and routed to rotation. Auto-escalation in 5m if unacked.

Maria (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Spinning up graphs and checking recent deploys. Noting p99 jump across us-east-1 only.

Maria (oncall): Quick metrics snapshot from dashboard:
```
p95: 210ms
p99: 1280ms
qps(avg): 380 -> 460
kv_cache_hit: 18% (down)
batcher.queue_length: 0.9k -> 3.8k
batcher.latency.p50: 35ms -> 210ms
batcher.latency.p99: 420ms -> 1500ms
errors(5m): 0.6% (timeouts ~504)
```

Jon SRE: I see a recent rollout (rollout #2023-11-15-1048) that changed default batch_size target from 64 -> 256 for the text-gen pool. That would explain queueing for short-latency traffic.

Anita (ML): Confirming — model-opt-v3 (deployed in that rollout) has slower per-token decode for short prompts when batching gets large due to attention kernel fallback. At high batch sizes it crosses an internal threshold and stalls.

Kevin (frontend): We're seeing customer-facing 504s on route /v1/generate for some tenants, notably AcmeCorp tests. Their telemetry shows requests timing out after 10s.

Maria (oncall): Mitigation plan 1) reduce batch size target, 2) apply routing policy to steer latency-sensitive traffic to small-v1 fallback, 3) scale up pool if needed. Doing step 1 now.

Maria (oncall): Running command:
```
./opsctl set-batcher-config --pool text-gen-east --target-batch 64 --reason "p99 spike"
```

AutoPagingBot: Command executed: set-batcher-config accepted (job id: jb-8891). Propagating config across 12 nodes (expected 30s).

Jon SRE: Autoscaler logs show it tried to add 2 nodes but failed with quota error: 
```
autoscaler: request to cloud api:  quota_exceeded (GPUs)
```
We might need manual add or change routing first.

Maria (oncall): Batcher config rolled out. Some improvement in queue length but p99 still elevated. Applying routing policy to move critical routes to fallback small model.

Maria (oncall): Running routing change:
```
./opsctl set-route-priority --route "/v1/generate" --pin-model small-v1 --weight 0.6
```

PagerDuty Bot: Note: manual scale recommended. If you need PD escalation to cloud quota team, trigger escalation.

Kevin (frontend): Can we triage AcmeCorp requests to the fallback immediately? Their SLA tests are failing.

Anita (ML): small-v1 has lower quality but consistent latency. Be mindful of regression. I'll add note to incidents doc.

Maria (oncall): Routing change applied. Observing metrics:
```
p99: 1280ms -> 920ms (initial)
batcher.queue_length: 3.8k -> 1.1k
kv_cache_hit: 18% -> 21%
```
Still above SLO but trending down.

Jon SRE: I'll try a manual scale to dedicated hot pool (if allowed) to relieve pressure while cloud team sorts quota. Attempting manual add of 2 g4dn-equivalent nodes to dedicated pool.

Jon SRE: Manual scale command output:
```
cloudctl create-instance --type g4dn.x2 --count 2 --tags=rg:inference-dedicated
-> created instances i-0a1b2c, i-0a1b2d
-> attaching to pool: text-gen-east-dedicated
```

AutoPagingBot: New instances attached. Routing will rebalance in ~45s.

Maria (oncall): After manual scale p99 now: 700ms, batcher length 400. Errors dropped to 0.15%. AcmeCorp tests show timeouts fall out.

Kevin (frontend): AcmeCorp reporting degraded but recovering. SE on the call got a follow-up note.

Anita (ML): Looking at model telemetry: model-opt-v3 shows increased memory pressure at batch sizes >200 which triggered internal CPU fallback kernels. We're flagging the rollout and preparing a patch to cap batch size by model automatically.

Maria (oncall): Action items so far:
- rollback config in the rollout to pin batch target back to 64 (done via set-batcher-config).
- routing pinned critical routes to small-v1 temporary.
- manual scale +2 nodes added to dedicated pool to relieve backlog.
- ML to produce a model-side guard for batch size.
- Cloud team to follow up on GPU quota increase request (opened PD ticket).

PagerDuty Bot: Noted. Escalation suppressed (incident acked). If SLO burn falls <110% for 15m, auto-close.

Maria (oncall): Customer impact: partial degradations for latency-sensitive customers in us-east; some 504s observed; no increased error-rate for embeddings or other regions. Affected tenants: AcmeCorp (tests), BetaApp internal QA. I notified their SE contacts.

Jon SRE: Handoff note for night oncall (starting 22:10 UTC):
- Current state: p99 ~ 700ms and falling. Routing pinned; manual nodes attached.
- Immediate risks: cloud quota still pending; if qps spikes again autoscaler might not be able to add nodes automatically.
- If p99 > 900ms for 10m: escalate to cloud-quota on call and consider moving non-critical traffic to eu/west region fallback.
- Runbook links: https://docs.redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-p99 and https://confluence.redwood/rollouts/batcher-guidelines

Maria (oncall): Handing off to Jon for the overnight window. I'll be available on DMs for any context.

Jon SRE: Taking over. I'll monitor dashboards and keep PD incident open until p99 < 350ms sustained for 30m or until cloud quota is resolved. Adding myself to incident notes.

Kevin (frontend): Thanks team. I'll patch the customer-facing status message to note degraded latency in us-east and that we're mitigating.

Anita (ML): I'll open a follow-up PR to add model-level batch cap and schedule a rollback of the rollout if we confirm regression in QA.

Maria (oncall): Closing adhoc timeline: mitigations applied in first 12m, manual scale done at +18m, routing pinned at +6m. Keeping incident alive for follow-up actions.

PagerDuty Bot: Incident acknowledged by Maria. Oncall owner: Jon SRE. Incident status: Mitigated -> monitoring.

Jon SRE: I'll file a post-incident ticket with root-cause analysis and recommended automation (auto cap by model + autoscaler fallback to region)."
